page: Microsoft Azure D12_v2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv2 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 4 physical cores with 4 vCPUs, allocating one thread per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 28.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 205 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the D12_v2 exhibits limited processing capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance is categorized as weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only operations scoring in the bottom 25%, though large-block write operations achieve average tier performance. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but overall compression and decompression speeds remain low.

From a resource density perspective, the D12_v2 offers a generous memory allocation of 7.0 GB per vCPU and bundled local storage, which may provide qualitative value for legacy workloads requiring memory capacity over raw compute speed. However, the tradeoff is significant: the older Intel Xeon architecture delivers lower performance per resource unit compared to modern cloud instances.

Given its performance profile, the D12_v2 is best suited for low-intensity general-purpose workloads, small-scale databases, basic web serving, or development and testing environments that require moderate memory capacity but do not demand high CPU throughput or rapid data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D12_v2 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine from the Dv2 family, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 physical cores, 4 vCPUs, 28.0 GB of RAM, and 205 GB of local storage, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance operates on the lower end of the spectrum, with single-core CPU and compression metrics in the bottom 10%, and multi-core and memory read bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory write bandwidth and small-model LLM text generation represent its stronger points, scoring in the average tier. Given these characteristics, the D12_v2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.0 GB per core but exhibits a clear tradeoff in processing speed. It is best suited for legacy applications, small databases, and moderate web serving workloads that prioritize memory capacity over high-performance compute.
